intro.author: Traditionally Matthew (also called Levi), the tax collector who became one of the Twelve (9:9; 10:3). The Gospel itself does not name its author.
intro.written: Debated: many scholars date it about AD 80–90; others place it before the temple fell in AD 70
intro.audience: Largely Jewish-Christian communities, possibly in Syria; Antioch is often suggested
intro.setting: Followers of Jesus and their Jewish neighbors were arguing over the same Scriptures and the same hope. Matthew writes to show that Jesus is the long-promised Messiah, the son of David and son of Abraham, and that the Hebrew Scriptures point to him.
intro.purpose: To present Jesus as Israel's Messiah and authoritative teacher, and to shape a community that obeys his teaching and carries it to all nations.
intro.bigIdea: Jesus is the promised King, God with us, whose kingdom is for every nation.
